evidence: Cic. Verr. 1.12: restituī in antīquum statum (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Fam. 3.11.4: reī pūblicae statum (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 2.47.5: quō locō rēs essent (Lewis & Short)
Hor. Ep. 1.12.25: quō sit Rōmāna locō rēs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: In aliquō locō esse, to be in a certain position or state (Lewis & Short s.v. locus); Cicero has the genitive, eōdem locī.

evidence: Masurius Sabinus in Gell. 4.20.11: male habitum … habitissimum (Lewis & Short s.v. habeō)
terms.comment: Of the body, a man’s or an animal’s; the superlative habitissimus, in excellent condition.

phrases.latin: rēs eōdem est locī quō relīquistī
phrases.english: things are in the same state as you left them

phrases.latin: Siciliam ita vexāvit ac perdidit ut ea restituī in antīquum statum nūllō modō possit
phrases.english: he so harried and ruined Sicily that it can never be put back in its former state
